/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
out=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 out.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n'+text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(out))
print(''.join(out)[:38000])
PY"

PY"

strengths: FALCON addresses a relevant continual segmentation problem: preserving previous classes while improving minority-class learning and distinguishing multiple unknown classes. Combining class prototypes with an adaptive cluster-membership model is a potentially useful contribution.

The empirical evaluation spans ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and Cityscapes, multiple incremental schedules, and CNN and Transformer architectures. Table 6 reports substantial improvements over FairCL within the Transformer category: 41.9 versus 37.6 mIoU on ADE20K 100-50 and 40.3 versus 35.5 on ADE20K 100-10.

The ablations provide meaningful evidence of practical benefits. In Table 1, the proposed loss improves minority-class mIoU from 26.4 to 30.8 while also improving majority-class performance on ADE20K 100-50. Table 2 supports adapting the visual grammar model, and Table 5 shows initial-class mIoU declining only from 44.9 to 44.4 across six stages.
The pipeline diagram, stagewise algorithm, and supplementary sensitivity studies help explain the implementation and its dependence on scaling, cluster margin, and neighborhood size.
weaknesses: The central fairness argument does not establish its claimed geometric consequences. Propositions 1–2 characterize normalized softmax probabilities, but a probability of 1/L does not imply that larger classes have more compact representations. Features can have identical projections onto a centroid while differing arbitrarily in orthogonal directions. Consequently, shrinking differences between these probabilities does not prove improved compactness or class fairness. Separately, Section 9 identifies the contrastive loss with a metric without establishing the triangle inequality; its subsequent Big-O manipulation does not establish the claimed knowledge-distillation upper bound.

The stated optimization leaves an important component unexplained. Equation (8) optimizes segmentation parameters, whereas R_C depends only on centroids described as frozen or updated through momentum; Section 9 explicitly treats centroids as constants during loss computation. Under that description, R_C has zero gradient with respect to the segmentation parameters, leaving its gains in Table 4 unexplained. Equation (4) also does not explicitly include the transition vector v in the denominator. If the denominator contains only image features, the loss is unbounded below in an unconstrained v, and Proposition 2's normalization assumption fails. These unresolved connections between the equations and actual training are decisive concerns despite the promising results.

The experiments only partially isolate the proposed mechanisms. Table 1 changes both the feature-loss scaling and the transition-vector term, without a matched reweighting control or comparison against the cited balanced contrastive objectives. Table 4 simultaneously removes visual grammar and reduces the number of unknown clusters to one; Table 2 does not specify whether cluster counts are held fixed. This limits attribution of gains to learned cluster topology. Since the attention architecture follows Clusformer [42], clearer separation of the adaptation's contribution is particularly important. Figure 6 provides qualitative evidence but no quantitative unknown-cluster assignment evaluation.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the supplementary optimizer settings. Missing details include DBSCAN parameters, selection of unknown pixels from background containing old and future classes, training durations, and the visual grammar pretraining procedure. The additional 12-layer attention model and repeated feature extraction are also not accompanied by runtime or memory comparisons, leaving the efficiency claims insufficiently supported.

Presentation issues are secondary: Table 3(a) uses VOC class-range headings for an ADE20K experiment, and several equation references in the proofs are incorrect. These are readily correctable and do not determine the recommendation.
